why: The identity was chosen by the operator from a specific identity sheet. These files are literal pixel crops of that sheet -- not redrawn, vectorized, recolored, sharpened, re-cropped or recompressed. A well-meant 'improvement' would replace an approved mark with an unapproved one that nobody signed off, and would look like a rendering difference rather than a substitution. So the bytes are pinned.
source: the operator-approved ARGUS identity sheet (retained by the project, not redistributed)
replacement_policy: A future vector trace must be approved against the raster source before it replaces any of these files. Changing a file here without updating this manifest fails the test suite. The villa header master is pinned the same way. Its DERIVATIVES are generated output: their hashes are recorded for reference and regenerated by the project's brand build (not part of this build), which refuses to run if the master does not match its declared sha256.

argus-mark.png.role: sidebar identity beside the ARGUS wordmark

argus-logo-primary.png.role: System / About screen and formal identity presentation; deliberately NOT repeated on every screen

argus-villa-header-v3-master.png.role: decorative header illustration, right-offset background atmosphere in the masthead
argus-villa-header-v3-master.png.approved_how: supplied by the operator WITH its sha256, which was verified before the file was copied. A header asset that silently became a different image is the easiest unnoticed substitution there is, because nobody reads a background.
argus-villa-header-v3-master.png.decorative_only: This is an ILLUSTRATION. It is not a photograph, a reconstruction, a measurement or a source, and it may NEVER be cited as scientific or historical evidence. It is rendered from CSS and carries no alt text, because a decorative image announced to a screen reader is noise.

composition.vesuvius_position: LEFT within the illustration, smoking, upper quadrant
composition.central_villa: symmetrical, pediment centred, pool on the central axis
composition.colonnades: both sides present and receding symmetrically

argus-villa-header-v3-master.png.placement: RIGHT-aligned and offset in the masthead at a contained height, not full-bleed: the left of the bar belongs to the mark and wordmark, and an illustration spanning the whole bar competes with the identity instead of sitting behind it. Suppressed entirely on a phone, where the masthead already wraps to protect the feed condition.
argus-villa-header-v3-master.png.transforms: NONE applied to the artwork. object-fit/background-size contain scales the whole frame, so nothing is stretched, flipped or cropped -- a cover crop would remove the left edge, which is the volcano.
